A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAM-H and WOFTSAM research despite the changed title and formatting. All pages, including appendices, figures, tables and equations, were readable and supported matching retained, relocated and changed content.

before.justification: v1 reports original POT-210 and PlanarTrack evaluations, component ablations, runtime measurements and ground-truth re-annotation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds MPOT-3K results, symmetry and Hough ablations, mask-fitting comparisons and cascade diagnostics.

M1.justification: The described pipeline retains SAM2+ segmentation, Hough boundary fitting, DINOv2 symmetry disambiguation, reduced-degree-of-freedom handling of partial visibility, and WOFTSAM's tracking/re-detection/fallback cascade. Additional explanations, ablated variants and experiments do not establish a revised proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds MPOT-3K evaluation alongside the retained POT-210 and PlanarTrack benchmarks, extending coverage to scenes containing multiple planar targets. Each object_id is tracked independently; this does not establish joint multiple-object tracking capability.

E2.justification: v2 Table S2 introduces minimum-area rectangle and Ramer-Douglas-Peucker mask-fitting baselines, plus SAM-H without DINO disambiguation. Section 4.1 also introduces a reported PRTrack comparison on MPOT-3K. Existing benchmark comparators remain; HVC-Net already participated in re-annotated PlanarTrack evaluation in v1 Figure S5.

E3.justification: The added MPOT-3K protocol tracks fixed object identities and reports p@50 alongside p@5/p@15, explicitly differing from PRTrack's Hungarian matching. New parameter sweeps and motion-only baseline controls extend the evaluation design. Appendix experiments use a newer computing stack; retained main benchmark settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds symmetry-consistency sensitivity, DINO removal, Hough parameter sensitivity, simple mask-fitting comparisons, a WOFTSAM segmentation-variant test, and cascade usage/rescue/failure diagnostics. The existing inlier-threshold study moves from v1 Table S1 to v2 Table 5. Conversely, v1's detailed PlanarTrack threshold/attribute curves and attribute-combination analysis disappear; its mirror case study is relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, performance error bars or formal significance tests. New diagnostic percentages and results from a different computing stack do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Headline POT-210 and PlanarTrack scores remain unchanged. v2 Table 2 adds MPOT-3K p@5/p@15/p@50 results: 67.0/89.9/95.1 for WOFTSAM and 54.2/81.2/89.9 for SAM-H. New ablation and cascade findings substantially expand the results. Appendix SAM-H scores of 62.4/80.5 use a newer stack, so they are not same-setting gains over 62.0/80.1. v1's detailed PlanarTrack curves and 67.1 p@5 oracle entry are omitted.

T1.justification: Section 3 changes the explicit pre-warp equations to use inverse homographies where v1 used forward homographies, correcting the transformation direction. Other geometric definitions and Hough calculations are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly foregrounds the training-free mask-to-homography formulation. It also corrects benchmark leadership claims: SAM-H leads PlanarTrack, while WOFTSAM leads POT-210 and exceeds prior PlanarTrack methods. v1's introduction and conclusion credited WOFTSAM with state-of-the-art performance on both.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of the new ablations and cascade diagnostics, explicitly discusses failures of the inlier-ratio heuristic, and qualifies MPOT-3K evaluation through matching and annotation limitations. It removes detailed discussion of indistinguishable distractors, texture-based symmetry ambiguities and contextual reasoning. The central quadrilateral, occlusion and complementarity limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new appendix experiments' A100/EPYC hardware and CUDA, cuDNN and PyTorch versions, plus per-frame RDP tuning and motion-only controls. Existing implementation and annotation instructions largely remain. Appendix B changes annotation-tool availability to a future release, conflicting with the retained publication claim in the conclusion; actual availability remains unresolved locally.

R1.justification: v2 adds and discusses the Multiple Planar Object Tracking work underlying PRTrack and MPOT-3K. It expands WOFT's description and emphasizes training-free geometric extraction from segmentation, while retaining most of the existing related-work coverage.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method explanation, results narrative, limitations and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Experiments are reorganized into main results, ablations, computational efficiency and annotation quality, with corresponding appendix restructuring. This substantially changes the narrative beyond simply inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation, with extensive float relocation and a redrawn cascade diagram. v1 Tables 2 and 3 are consolidated into v2 Table 1, and several experimental tables are added. Appendix examples move into the main text, while v1 Figures S5/S6 disappear. v2 Figure 10 redisplays an existing occlusion example.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports the unchanged method through direct DINO ablation evidence (80.5 versus 68.0 p@15 in Table S2), sensitivity tests and cascade diagnostics, and corrects benchmark leadership claims. These improve v1's already substantial evaluation. The gain is moderated by removing detailed PlanarTrack analyses, comparing MPOT methods under different matching protocols, and using motion-only disambiguation for mask-fitting baselines, which limits attribution of their performance gaps.
